# United Autism Therapy

> United Autism Therapy Inc. provides in-home ABA (Applied Behavior Analysis) therapy for children with autism in Westminster, California, with in-home services across Orange, Riverside, San Diego, San Bernardino & Santa Clara Counties. Programs are designed and supervised by Board Certified Behavior Analysts (BCBAs) and delivered with Registered Behavior Technicians (RBTs), with parent training included. Supporting Children. Empowering Families.

## Key facts
- Address: 13571 Beach Blvd, Westminster, CA 92683
- Phone: (714) 709-7819
- Hours: Monday–Saturday 8:00 AM–6:00 PM; closed Sunday
- Service area: Westminster, CA; in-home services in Orange County, Riverside County, San Diego County, San Bernardino County, Santa Clara County, California
- Insurance: many plans, including Medi-Cal, cover ABA for children with an autism diagnosis; coverage varies by plan
- Does not provide autism diagnostic evaluations
- First step: free consultation (https://unitedautismcenter.com/contact/)

## Services
- [ABA Therapy](https://unitedautismcenter.com/services/aba-therapy/): Individualized, play-based Applied Behavior Analysis designed by BCBAs around your child and family goals.
- [Speech & Language Therapy](https://unitedautismcenter.com/services/speech-language-therapy/): Helping children develop verbal and non-verbal communication so they can express themselves.
- [Occupational Therapy](https://unitedautismcenter.com/services/occupational-therapy/): Building independence through fine motor development, sensory support and self-care skills.

## Ways to receive ABA
- [In-Home ABA Therapy](https://unitedautismcenter.com/services/in-home-aba/): BCBA-designed ABA therapy in your home, built around your child’s everyday routines, with parents coached along the way.
- [Parent Training](https://unitedautismcenter.com/services/parent-training/): Practical coaching so you can support your child’s progress in everyday life, not just during sessions.
- [Center-Based ABA](https://unitedautismcenter.com/services/center-based-aba/): Structured, play-based sessions at our Westminster center with built-in opportunities to practice social skills.
- [School-Based ABA](https://unitedautismcenter.com/services/school-based-aba/): Support in the classroom so your child can practice learning, social and routine skills with teachers and peers.

## ABA Therapy articles
- [BCBA vs RBT: Who Does What on Your Child's ABA Team](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/bcba-vs-rbt/): A BCBA (Board Certified Behavior Analyst) holds a graduate-level certification, assesses your child, writes the ABA treatment plan, and supervises the team. An RBT (Registered Behavior Technician) holds a paraprofessional certification and works directly with your child in sessions, following the BCBA's plan under close, ongoing supervision. Both credentials are issued by the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB).
- [ABA Data Collection: How Your Child's Team Tracks Progress and Adjusts the Plan](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/data-driven-aba-therapy/): ABA data collection means recording how a child performs on each therapy goal during sessions, such as how often a skill happens or how much help was needed. A Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) reviews that data, often as graphs, to decide whether to continue, change, or move past a goal. Data keeps decisions based on evidence rather than guesswork.
- [Positive Reinforcement in ABA: What It Is and How It Helps Kids Learn](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/positive-reinforcement-in-aba/): Positive reinforcement in ABA means adding something your child values right after a behavior, so that behavior is more likely to happen again. The reinforcer might be praise, a favorite toy, a short activity, or a choice. The BACB ethics code asks behavior analysts to prioritize positive reinforcement procedures, and reinforcers are individualized and faded over time.
- [ABA Therapy Goals: Real Examples and How Your Child's Team Sets Them](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/aba-therapy-goals/): ABA therapy goals are specific, measurable skills a child works toward, chosen from an assessment and the family's priorities. Common areas include communication, social and play skills, daily living, independence, and learning readiness. A Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) writes each goal so progress can be tracked, and updates goals as the child grows.
- [How Long Does ABA Therapy Last? Hours, Timelines, and Progress](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/how-long-does-aba-therapy-last/): How long does ABA therapy last? How BCBAs set weekly hours, what affects session length and timelines, how progress is reviewed, and how therapy winds down.
- [Why Is ABA Therapy Controversial? History, Criticism, and Change](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/is-aba-therapy-controversial/): Why is ABA therapy controversial? An honest look at its history, autistic self-advocates' concerns, how the field has changed, and what to ask about care.
- [What Age to Start ABA Therapy, From Toddlers to Teens](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/what-age-to-start-aba-therapy/): What age to start ABA therapy? Why early support helps, what ABA looks like for toddlers, preschoolers, school-age kids, and teens, and why it's never too late.
- [How to Choose an ABA Provider: A Parent's Checklist of Questions](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/how-to-choose-an-aba-provider/): How to choose an ABA provider: a checklist of questions to ask about credentials, goals, your child's dignity, and insurance, plus red and green flags.
- [Benefits of ABA Therapy for Children, and Its Limits](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/benefits-of-aba-therapy/): The benefits of ABA therapy for children, from communication to daily living and safety skills, plus honest limitations and what to watch for in a program.
- [Center-Based vs. In-Home ABA Therapy: Which Setting Fits Your Child?](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/center-based-vs-in-home-aba-therapy/): Compare center-based vs in-home ABA therapy: social opportunities, generalization, family involvement, logistics, and when a hybrid plan makes sense.
- [How Does ABA Therapy Work? The Process, Step by Step](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/how-does-aba-therapy-work/): How does ABA therapy work? Follow the process from first consultation to reassessment, and learn the core techniques BCBAs use to help children build skills.
- [What Is ABA Therapy? A Clear Guide for Parents](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/what-is-aba-therapy/): What is ABA therapy? A plain-language guide for parents on what ABA stands for, how it helps kids build skills, who provides it, and what modern ABA looks like.

## In-Home ABA articles
- [How to Start In-Home ABA Therapy: A Step-by-Step Guide for Parents](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/how-to-start-in-home-aba-therapy/): To start in-home ABA therapy, most families follow five steps: a first consultation with a provider, an insurance benefits check and authorization, an assessment by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), a written treatment plan with individualized goals, and scheduling regular home sessions. A diagnosis or referral from a qualified professional is usually needed, and timelines vary by insurance plan.
- [Preparing Your Home for In-Home ABA Therapy: A Practical Checklist](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/preparing-your-home-for-aba/): Preparing your home for in-home ABA usually means choosing a small, consistent session space, doing a quick safety check, setting aside a few favorite toys and snacks, planning a regular session time, and making sure an adult will be home. You do not need special equipment or a perfect house. Your child's therapy team will help you adjust the setup as they learn your child.
- [ABA in Everyday Family Routines: Mealtime, Play, Dressing and More](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/aba-in-everyday-family-routines/): ABA in daily routines means teaching skills during the ordinary moments of family life, such as meals, play, bath time, getting dressed, moving between activities, and simple chores. In in-home ABA, a therapist picks a few of these moments, breaks the routine into small steps, and uses your child's interests to make practice meaningful. Parents learn to use the same steps so skills carry over.
- [Benefits of In-Home ABA Therapy: What Learning at Home Can Offer](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/benefits-of-in-home-aba-therapy/): The main benefits of in-home ABA therapy are that your child learns in a familiar place, practices skills during the real routines where they are needed, and has family members nearby to learn the same strategies. Home sessions can also make it easier for skills to carry over into daily life and can reduce travel. Results vary, and the right plan depends on your child's goals.
- [What Happens During an In-Home ABA Session? A Walkthrough for Parents](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/what-happens-in-an-aba-therapy-session/): During an in-home ABA session, a therapist comes to your home and works with your child on individualized goals through play and everyday routines like snack, getting dressed, and clean-up. A typical session includes a warm-up to build rapport, short teaching moments built into activities your child enjoys, breaks, ongoing data collection, and a brief check-in with the parent at the end.

## Autism articles
- [Autism Meltdown vs. Tantrum: How to Tell the Difference and Help Your Child](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/autism-meltdown-vs-tantrum/): A tantrum is usually goal-directed: a child wants something, and the tantrum often stops once they get it or the audience leaves. A meltdown is a response to overwhelm, from sensory overload, stress, or sudden change. It isn't a choice and often continues regardless of what happens around it. During a meltdown, focus on safety, calm, and fewer words, not consequences.
- [Daily Living Skills for Children With Autism: A Practical Guide for Parents](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/daily-living-skills-autism/): Daily living skills for children with autism are the practical self-care and household tasks that build independence, such as dressing, washing hands, brushing teeth, eating with utensils, toileting, and helping clean up. They are usually taught by breaking each task into small steps, using visual supports, and practicing at the times and places the skill is actually needed, often at home.
- [Social Skills for Children With Autism: What Helps and How ABA Can Support It](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/autism-social-skills/): Social skills for children with autism are the everyday ways a child connects with others, such as taking turns, joining play, sharing attention, asking for help, and holding a short back-and-forth. They are taught best in small steps, during real play and routines, and around goals that matter to the child and family. ABA, speech therapy, and social skills groups can all support this work.
- [Early Intervention for Autism: Why It Matters and How to Start](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/early-intervention-for-autism/): What early intervention for autism includes, why starting early can help, and how California Early Start works for babies and toddlers from birth to age 3.
- [Autism Evaluation for Kids: When to Get One and What to Expect](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/when-to-get-an-autism-evaluation/): A parent's guide to autism evaluation for kids: when to consider one, screening vs. diagnosis, who diagnoses autism, how to prepare, and paths in Orange County.
- [Early Signs of Autism in Babies and Toddlers: A Guide by Age](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/early-signs-of-autism/): Learn the early signs of autism by age, from 9 months to 5 years, what repetitive behaviors can look like, and what to do next if you have a concern.
- [Understanding Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/understanding-autism-spectrum-disorder/): A plain-language guide to autism spectrum disorder in children: the two core areas, what support levels mean, co-occurring conditions and what helps.

## Parent Resources articles
- [How to Get an IEP for Your Autistic Child in Orange County](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/iep-for-autism-orange-county/): An IEP (Individualized Education Program) is a written plan for special education services that public schools provide to eligible children ages 3 to 21. To start, send your school district a written request for a special education assessment. In California, the district generally has 15 days to send an assessment plan, and an IEP meeting is held within 60 days of your signed consent, not counting long school breaks.
- [Autism and Sleep Routines: How to Build Calmer Nights at Home](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/autism-and-sleep-routines/): Sleep problems are common in autistic children. Experts recommend checking first for medical causes, then building a calm, predictable bedtime routine: the same steps in the same order, a visual schedule, a consistent wake time, and a sleep space that suits your child's senses. If sleep stays hard after a few consistent weeks, talk with your pediatrician before trying supplements like melatonin.
- [How to Get ABA Therapy Covered by Insurance: A Step-by-Step Guide](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/how-to-start-aba-through-insurance/): To get ABA therapy covered by insurance, most families follow the same path: get an autism diagnosis or a referral from a physician or psychologist, confirm the plan's behavioral health benefits, choose an in-network ABA provider, get the assessment authorized, and then get the treatment plan authorized. Authorization is usually reviewed again periodically, so keep copies of every document.
- [How Parents Can Support ABA Therapy at Home: Practical Strategies](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/supporting-aba-therapy-at-home/): How parents can support ABA therapy at home with routines, visual schedules, first-then language, and daily practice, plus when to check in with your BCBA.
- [Autism Support for Parents in Orange County: Where to Start](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/autism-support-orange-county-parents/): A practical roadmap to autism support for parents in Orange County: screening, Regional Center of Orange County, school IEPs, health plans, therapy and support.
- [Does Medi-Cal Cover ABA Therapy? What California Parents Should Know](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/does-medi-cal-cover-aba-therapy/): Does Medi-Cal cover ABA therapy? Learn who qualifies for behavioral health treatment, how to get started with your plan, and what to ask about authorization.

## Speech & Communication articles
- [AAC and Autism: How Alternative Communication Helps Your Child](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/aac-and-autism/): What AAC is for autistic children, from picture boards to speech apps, why it does not stop speech, how modeling works, and how families can get started.
- [Speech Therapy for Autism: How It Helps and What to Expect](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/speech-therapy-for-autism/): How speech therapy for autism works: what SLPs do, echolalia, AAC, what sessions look like, how it fits with ABA, and simple activities to try at home.

## Occupational Therapy articles
- [Sensory Processing and Autism: Understanding Your Child's Senses](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/sensory-processing-and-autism/): What sensory processing differences in autism look like, sensory seeking vs avoiding, meltdowns vs tantrums, and calming strategies for home and outings.
- [Occupational Therapy for Autism: Skills, Goals, and Home Activities](https://unitedautismcenter.com/blog/occupational-therapy-for-autism/): How occupational therapy for autism builds fine motor, self-care, sensory, and play skills, what an OT evaluation involves, and activities to try at home.
